KY-2026-SB66.aiSummary: Kentucky law now expands the list of drugs tied to impaired driving rules to include clonazepam, cyclobenzaprine, and fentanyl. It also requires people to be told that refusing a requested blood test can lead to a driver’s license suspension, and that a conviction under the law will also bring a suspension. The Transportation Cabinet must destroy records of moving traffic convictions that are more than 10 years old.

KY-2026-SB129.aiSummary: This law changes how much employers pay into the service capacity upgrade fund for unemployment insurance. It lowers the rate by 0.075% through December 31, 2026, then changes the rate formula starting January 1, 2027. The Education and Labor Cabinet secretary must set the yearly adjustment for each year after that, up to 1.025%.

KY-2026-SR305.title: A RESOLUTION censuring Kentucky Supreme Court Justice Kelly Thompson for his intemperate remarks that threatened attorneys and legislators participating in pending impeachment proceedings with professional discipline and criminal prosecution, and directing a complaint to be filed against him with the Judicial Conduct Commission.

KY-2026-SR305.aiSummary: The Senate adopted a resolution censuring Kentucky Supreme Court Justice Kelly Thompson for remarks tied to pending impeachment proceedings. KY-2026-SB312.aiSummary: The bill would let certified court security officers transport people who are being detained or are in custody when a court orders it. It would also make changes so these officers can transport some people in mental health cases under set rules.

KY-2026-SB156.policyArea: Children And Minors, Civil Actions, County Clerks
KY-2026-SB156.aiSummary: The bill would bar marriage for anyone under 18 in Kentucky and stop county clerks from issuing marriage licenses to people under 18. It would also end the court process that lets 17-year-olds ask permission to marry. Marriages already entered into in Kentucky before the bill takes effect, and marriages entered into in another state or country, would be treated differently under the bill.

KY-2026-SB141.title: AN ACT relating to legal advertisements.
KY-2026-SB141.summary: Amend KRS 424.110 to define "advertisement" and "published statement of ownership"; amend KRS 424.120 to determine where newspaper advertisements shall be placed when 2 or more newspapers meet the initial qualifications; determine when alternative publication procedures may be used when there is no newspaper in the county containing the government seeking to make the advertisement or no suitable newspaper in an adjoining similarly sized county; define "adjoining similarly sized county", and set publication parameters for advertisements, along with parallel advertising in the largest association of newspapers within the Commonwealth; set time requirements for publication; provide when digital newspapers may be used for advertising and when publication is deemed to have occurred; amend KRS 424.147 to expand remedial advertising to satisfy not only the provisions found in KRS Chapter 424, but the remainder of the Kentucky Revised Statutes relating to timing or manner of publication; amend KRS 424.160 to set the rates for advertising; require contractual terms offered to public agencies of the Commonwealth that are offered to commercial customers; require the rate charged by a newspaper shall be the lowest advertising rate provided for in KRS 424.215; provide volume discounts for display forms; amend KRS 132.027, 68.245, 132.023, and 160.470 to specify that publication shall be made in the qualified newspaper under KRS 424.120 rather than in the largest newspaper within the county; remove the requirement for display type and column inch minimum; expand the requirement that publication be made not less than 7 days nor more than 21 days.

KY-2026-HB535.title: AN ACT relating to investor-owned electric utilities and declaring an emergency.
KY-2026-HB535.summary: Amend KRS 278.670 to define "environmental control" and "underpreciated extra-state generation utility plant balances," amend various definitions, and make technical changes; amend KRS 278.672 to remove the deadline date for calculating the value of the regulatory asset associated with the undepreciated extra-state generation utility plant balances, deferred storm costs, and other regulatory assets approved by the Public Service Commission (PSC) remove the dollar amount thresholds for qualifying for a financing order; remove the submittals associated with securitization of deferred costs for retried electric generation greater than 50%; add additional submittals for an application for a financing order; add requirement for a utility to acquire in-state dispatchable generation and agree to a freeze on base rates for a period of 2 years; define "dispatchable"; amend KRS 278.674 to prohibit the PSC from requiring securitized bonds to be marketed as a specific type of security or that an assignee be formed as a specific type of entity; provide a price cap for costs associated with retaining counsel, advisors, or other consultants; remove PSC authority to address how the securities are marketed; add a template issuance advice letter to be included in the financing order; direct that the PSC must approve sales or transfer of assets including extra-state generation facilities even if the balances are securitized; amend KRS 278.678 to make technical changes; amend KRS 278.682 to remove the requirement that the securitized surcharge be listed as a separate item on the customer bill; EMERGENCY.

KY-2026-HB535.policyArea: Effective Dates, Emergency, Energy, Environment And Conservation
KY-2026-HB535.aiSummary: The bill would change rules for investor-owned electric utilities and the state utility commission. It would set new terms for utility financing, including rules for securitized bonds, and would require a utility to seek in-state dispatchable power, meaning electric generation that can be turned on when needed, along with a 2-year freeze on base rates. It would also change how some storm, generation, and other costs can be handled, and it would let the commission approve sales or transfers of certain utility assets even if the costs are being repaid through securitized bonds.

KY-2026-HB397.title: AN ACT relating to trophy catfish.
KY-2026-HB397.summary: Create a new section of KRS Chapter 150 to define terms; require that any permit issued to take a lower Ohio River trophy catfish shall expire on May 31, 2027; prohibit the issuance or reissuance of an any lower Ohio River trophy catfish permits after that date; after the effective date of the Act, prohibit the transfer or reissuance of any lower Ohio River trophy catfish permit; prohibit the transportation of live trophy catfish except by boat while in the course of legally fishing; amend KRS 150.990 to make a violation of the prohibition on transporting live trophy catfish a Class A misdemeanor for the first offense and a Class D felony for each subsequent offense.
KY-2026-HB397.summarySource: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)

KY-2026-HB397.policyArea: Boats And Boating, Corrections Impact, Crimes And Punishments
KY-2026-HB397.aiSummary: The bill would set rules for lower Ohio River trophy catfish permits, including making any current permit expire on May 31, 2027. After the act takes effect, those permits could not be transferred or reissued, and new ones could not be issued after that date. It would also bar most transport of live trophy catfish, except by boat while fishing, and make breaking that rule a misdemeanor for the first offense and a felony for later offenses.

KY-2026-HB298.summary: Amend KRS 164.7874, relating to KEES awards, to define terms; amend KRS 164.7879 to establish the use of a specified equivalent grade point average for eligible graduates of certain private, parochial, or church schools based on the Advanced Placement exam score, dual credit courses grade point average, or a combination of both; amend KRS 164.7881 and 164.7884 to conform.
KY-2026-HB298.summarySource: Kentucky legislature, Summary of Original Version (via Open States)
KY-2026-HB298.policyArea: Education, Elementary And Secondary, Education, Finance, Education, Higher
KY-2026-HB298.aiSummary: The bill would change rules for KEES college scholarship awards for students from certain private, parochial, or church schools. It would set how an equal grade point average is figured using Advanced Placement exam scores, dual credit course grades, or both. It would also update related school and scholarship laws to match these changes.
